preamble: In the Moldavian dialect of Romanian, labials are palatalized before front vowels and glides, and the palatalized bilabial [pʲ] then shifts its closure from the lips to the palate, becoming the palatal stop [c] (spelled ch in dialect writing). The voiced [bʲ] and the nasal [mʲ] develop the same way, to [ɟ] and [ɲ]. The result is a well-known stereotype of Moldavian speech, absent from standard Romanian. No comparable regular pʲ > c change has been verified outside Eastern Romance.

examples.note: Initial p before a front glide becomes the palatal stop.
The change also applies word-internally; Wikipedia also records [kop̚ˈkʲil] with a residual labial closure.
The same change before the front vowels i and e.
